models_evaluated: off-the-shelf cloud-based random forest non-attendance risk model

links.outcome: Staff ability to act on model risk scores within defined workflow roles
links.effect: Many staff struggled to action the intervention workflow, especially when it was not seen to fall within their defined roles; low volumes of intervention calls were made in phase 1 and call rates were lower in phase 2.
links.quote: Thematic analysis of the qualitative data suggests that many staff delivering the intervention struggled with actioning the intervention workflow, especially when it was not seen to fall within their defined roles.

links.outcome: Team capacity and prioritisation to act on predictive model outputs
links.effect: Differing prioritisation of the intervention amid long waiting lists and staff resourcing issues limited pilot success; only 3 of 9 services significantly reduced non-attendance in phase 1, and 1 in phase 2 (20.4% to 19.1%, p<0.05).
links.quote: Differing perceptions of how the intervention should be prioritised, especially in the context of long waiting lists and staff resourcing issues, offer some context to the limits of the pilot's success.

screen.reason: Empirical mixed-methods evaluation of an operational predictive model pilot for outpatient non-attendance in the NHS, evaluating workflow adoption and non-attendance rates without comparing specific deployment practices or safeguards.
